claude.sample_unit: procedures (institutional EHR cohort; plus 301,999 registry procedures)
models_evaluated: Elastic-net logistic regression pediatric SSI prediction model (NSQIP-Pediatric-derived)

links.outcome: Discrimination and calibration of registry-derived model on local EHR data
links.effect: Direct application to institutional EHR cohort: c-statistic 0.60, Brier 0.07, calibration slope 0.15, O/E 0.25, versus registry c-statistic 0.75 and slope 1.00.
links.quote: Direct application to the institutional EHR cohort produced inflated predicted risk and poor performance, with c-statistic 0.60, Brier score 0.07, calibration slope 0.15, and O/E ratio 0.25.

links.outcome: Calibration after logistic recalibration in local EHR cohort
links.effect: Logistic recalibration restored calibration slope and O/E ratio to 1.00 after predictor harmonization (slope 0.81, O/E 1.35 beforehand).
links.quote: Logistic recalibration restored calibration slope and O/E ratio to 1.00.

links.outcome: Compatibility of model predictor definitions with EHR data
links.effect: Diagnosis-code predictor misalignment between registry and EHR degraded performance; omitting open-ended diagnosis-code indicators improved c-statistic to 0.70, Brier 0.03, slope 0.81, O/E 1.35.
links.quote: After omitting open-ended diagnosis-code indicators, performance improved, with c-statistic 0.70, Brier score 0.03, calibration slope 0.81, and O/E ratio 1.35.

links.outcome: Performance in temporally distinct registry cohort versus new institutional setting
links.effect: Performance preserved in temporally distinct registry cohort (c-statistic 0.75, slope 1.00, O/E 1.01) but not directly transportable to the institutional EHR.
links.quote: Performance was preserved in the registry cohort, with c-statistic 0.75, Brier score 0.03, calibration slope 1.00, and observed/expected (O/E) ratio 1.01.

unlisted_practices: Closed testing procedure to select recalibration strategy

links.effect: Models performing well under internal or registry validation were not directly transportable to real-world EHR environments.
links.quote: These findings highlight a key challenge for clinical translation: models that perform well under internal or registry-based validation may not be directly transportable to real-world EHR environments.

links.effect: Predictor misalignment across registry and EHR data emerged as a key barrier to direct institutional deployment.
links.quote: Predictor misalignment-differences in how model predictors were captured and measured across registry and EHR data-emerged as a key barrier to direct institutional deployment, underscoring the importance of implementation-aware external validation before clinical use.

screen.reason: Evaluates institutional transportability, predictor harmonization, and local recalibration strategies to adapt a registry-trained surgical site infection model to local EHR data prior to clinical deployment.
